unit.title: Launch: Proficiency Goals & the Seal of Biliteracy

contentBlocks.text: Everything this week has been building to one thing: a written commitment, in Spanish, to a specific proficiency target — not a vague hope, a real goal you're sealing today and reopening at the end of the year to measure against.

[[la meta a largo plazo]] — a long-term goal — only works if it's specific. 'I want to be good at Spanish' isn't a meta a largo plazo; it's a wish. A real one names three things: the exact ACTFL level you're aiming for, a realistic timeline, and the concrete actions you'll actually take to get there. This course's own trajectory gives you a built-in timeline to anchor to: Intermediate Low by around 11th grade, and Intermediate Mid — the actual Seal of Biliteracy threshold from Tuesday's lesson — by senior year. You don't have to commit to exactly that pace today, but it's a realistic, research-backed target to measure your own goal against.

Use these sentence starters to build your goal statement — mixing English and Spanish is completely fine this week; you'll get more comfortable staying in Spanish as the year goes on:

Mi meta a nivel de dominio es... (My proficiency goal is...)
Quiero lograr esto para... (I want to achieve this by [timeframe]...)
Para lograrlo, voy a... (To achieve this, I'm going to...) — name 2-3 real actions: practicing outside class, watching a show in Spanish, keeping a vocabulary journal, talking with a Spanish-speaking family member or neighbor, etc.
Esto es importante para mí porque... (This matters to me because...)

Save what you write today — literally. At the end of this year, you'll read it again next to a new recording of your own Spanish, the same way today's lesson compared two different speakers. That comparison is the whole point of a baseline. Next week: identity and heritage, the first real conversation topic of the year.

objectives: Write a specific proficiency goal statement in Spanish naming a target ACTFL level, timeline, and concrete actions
Connect this week's proficiency-scale and Seal-of-Biliteracy content into a personal, motivating commitment
materialsNeeded: Optional: a phone or recording device, if the family wants to keep a personal audio keepsake of today's goal statement for comparison at year's end (not required, and not stored on the platform)
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review the week briefly: Novice vs. Intermediate (Day 1), the Seal of Biliteracy and credit crosswalk (Day 2), the self-assessment baseline (Days 3-4).
2. Read the sentence-starter template together.
3. Have the student draft answers to each starter on the worksheet before combining them into one paragraph.
4. Encourage the student to name a specific, personally realistic timeline rather than copying the course's default pace exactly.
5. Optional: record the finished goal statement being read aloud, purely as a family keepsake — this isn't uploaded or stored anywhere by the platform.
6. File the finished statement somewhere it will actually be found again at year's end.
7. Preview next week's topic: identity and heritage.
differentiationTips: Struggling: if naming a specific ACTFL level feels too abstract, let them anchor to a plain-language version instead — 'able to have a real conversation about my day' — and translate that into Intermediate-level language together afterward
Ready for more: have them research one concrete way Spanish proficiency could matter for a career or college path they're actually interested in, and fold that into the 'porque' (why) section
Keep this low-pressure and genuinely personal — an honest, modest goal the student will actually work toward beats an impressive-sounding one they'll abandon by week three
teacherGuide.answerKey: There is no single correct goal statement — evaluate for specificity (a named ACTFL level or clear plain-language equivalent), a realistic timeline, at least two concrete actions, and a genuine personal reason, per today's template.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Closes the week's WA-WL-2015.5.2 (Communities: Lifelong Learning) arc by turning the week's factual content — the proficiency scale (Day 1), the Seal of Biliteracy and credit law (Day 2), and the self-assessed baseline (Days 3-4) — into a personally authored commitment, exactly the 'own the path to it' framing the scope-and-sequence names for this standard tag.

generationData.instructions: Draft your proficiency goal statement using the sentence starters from today's lesson. Write your answers in Spanish where you can.

prompts.prompt: Mi meta a nivel de dominio es... (What ACTFL level are you aiming for, and by when?)
Para lograrlo, voy a... (List 2-3 concrete actions you'll actually do this year.)
Esto es importante para mí porque... (Why does this goal matter to you personally?)
Now combine your answers above into one complete goal statement paragraph, in Spanish.
